concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - new entry in the version:server-* family; not previously in the registry (which had 6.5, 6.6.1, 7.0, 7.2, 7.6, 8.0) - the release that introduced multi-CA trust stores

relations.subject: cert:multiple-root-certificates
relations.evidence: Prior to Couchbase Server Version 7.1, a Couchbase-Server cluster could maintain at most _one_ root certificate: all nodes and all clients were obliged to rely on this certificate's authority. From version 7.1, Couchbase Server permits multiple root certificates to be maintained in a _trust store_ for the cluster.

notable_absence.finding: The illustration builds a worked example with ten CAs in one cluster's trust store ('CA a' through 'CA j'), but the page never states whether there is a maximum number of root or intermediate certificates a trust store can hold, or any operational guidance on trust-store size (performance impact of chain-of-trust resolution against a large trust store, for example). Ten looks illustrative rather than a stated ceiling, but the page leaves this genuinely open.

cross_component_finding: This page and certificates.md cross-reference each other constantly (four separate links back to certificates.md's #intermediate-certificates and #node-certificate anchors) and are clearly written as one continuous topic split across two files for length, not two independent concepts - the split itself produces no new ontology content, only shared vocabulary (cert:trust-store, cert:root-certificate, cert:intermediate-certificate, cert:node-certificate, cert:client-certificate) reused wholesale from the sibling page.
